## Motivation

Depends on #46600 (the CUDA MoE noise fix, which fixes #46461). This PR will be rebased on it once it lands, so the fix commit below will drop out of the diff.

Changes for HunyuanImage-3 (the prefix K/V cache is the main one; the opt-in FA3 attention and the `cot_text` fix are described under Modifications):

1. **Fix: generation on CUDA produced a noise texture** (on main too). The MoE block ran the routed experts before the shared MLP. On CUDA the Triton `FusedMoE` path runs in place (`inplace=True` by default) and overwrites `hidden_states` with the expert output, so the shared MLP read the expert output instead of the layer input and every MoE layer was wrong. The NPU path (AscendTPDispatcher) is not in place, which is likely why the original NPU validation in #36311 did not see it; the cookbook also marks the CUDA recipe as unverified. srt's own Hunyuan model already runs the shared MLP first.
2. **Perf: cache the text prefix K/V across denoising steps.** HunyuanImage-3 recomputes the whole text prefix through every layer (attention and MoE) on every step, even though that prefix never changes. The proposal this implements:

> **P1. Prefix KV cache** (`hunyuan_image3.py`: `ImageKVCacheManager`, `forward_block`)
> The text prefix is causal and step-invariant. At `first_step`, keep the per-layer prefix K/V; on later steps feed only the image tokens as queries and attend to [cached prefix K/V, image K/V]. Replace the dense 4-D bool-mask SDPA with FA varlen (prefix causal + image full) or flex.
> Removes L_text/(L_text+L_img) of the MoE compute per step. Large for long or "think" prompts; also recovers FlashAttention.

This PR does the prefix K/V cache with the dense SDPA as the default, plus the FA varlen part as an opt-in (`--attention-backend fa3`), since FA3 is not bitwise equal to SDPA. The official model does the same caching at inference (later steps feed only the timestep and image tokens against a static KV cache).

## Modifications

**Fix (commit 2)**
- `hunyuan_image3.py`: `HunYuanSparseMoeBlock.forward` runs the shared MLP before the in-place experts.
- `pipelines/hunyuan_image3.py`: match the official `FlowMatchDiscreteScheduler` schedule, `shift(linspace(1, 0, N + 1))[:-1]` (`use_uniform_sigmas=True`). The old setup shifted the training-sigma range a second time; for 10 steps the last timestep was 8.93 instead of 250.

**Prefix K/V cache (commit 1)**
- `hunyuan_image3_utils.py`: `ImageKVCacheManager` stores each layer's prefix K/V on step 0, keyed by a cache slot, and on later steps prepends it to the suffix K/V. Adds `split_suffix_inputs` and `pad_prefix_rows`.
- `hunyuan_image3.py`: `forward_block` takes `prefix_len` and `cache_slot`. Step 0 runs the full sequence; later steps run only the suffix rows and pad the output back to full length, so callers see the same shape.
- `ar_stage.py`: computes the prefix once as the rows before the first noisy-image or timestep token, and returns no prefix (full compute) when a clean image block straddles that boundary. `first_step` is now `step_idx == 0` (it was always `True`, and nothing read it). CFG cond and uncond use separate cache slots, since they run as two backbone calls on the same modules.
- Falls back to the current path when CLA is on, when the cache-dit adapter drives the blocks, or when no safe prefix exists.

Why the cache is exact: the mask is causal, so every row before the first varying token only sees prompt and clean conditioning tokens. Clean conditioning images before the noisy block are cached too, so the saving is a bit larger than L_text/(L_text+L_img).

Memory cost of the cache: `bs x P x kv_heads x head_dim x 4 bytes` per layer per CFG slot. Measured 156 MB per GPU for a 1,248-token prefix with both CFG slots (exactly the formula); the reported peak is unchanged.

**Opt-in FA3 segment attention (`--attention-backend fa3`)**
- `hunyuan_image3_utils.py`: `build_attention_segments` splits the mask (causal text, bidirectional image blocks) into `(start, end, causal)` segments; `segmented_attention` runs one FA3 varlen call per segment with bottom-right causal alignment, for both full and cached-suffix steps. GQA is native, so no `repeat_kv`. Hopper only; elsewhere the masked SDPA path is kept.
- `ar_stage.py` / `pipelines/hunyuan_image3.py`: segments are built only when `attention_backend == "fa"` (what `fa3`/`fa4` resolve to). The default path is unchanged and still bitwise identical to main + fix.
- 2x H200: 22.6 s vs 26.8 s for the default path (1.55x vs main + fix). Not bitwise: PSNR 21-24 dB vs SDPA, same composition. On GPU the segments reproduce the attention mask exactly over 384 calls and FA3 vs SDPA differs by at most one bf16 ulp per call, so the drift is kernel rounding compounding over layers and steps. Details and images: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46454#issuecomment-6422227024

**Fix: `cot_text` from the image API**
- `configs/sample/hunyuan_image3.py`: declare `bot_task`, `system_prompt` and `cot_text` in `image_request_extra_fields`. The image endpoint only forwards declared fields, so think/recaption text was silently dropped. With it, think prompts are 1.32x to 1.50x faster than main + fix (the reasoning text lands in the cached prefix), outputs identical: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46454#issuecomment-6422648092

## How the noise bug was found

On 2x H200 TP2 with debug-only instrumentation (not in this PR):
- Checked the port line by line against the official `modeling_hunyuan_image_3.py` and `hunyuan_image_3_pipeline.py` shipped with the checkpoint. 2D RoPE, QKV split, QK norm order, SwiGLU half order, residual flow, UNetDown/UNetUp, timestep embedders, CFG, Euler step and VAE decode all match.
- Compared real decoder layers at step 0 against an fp32 reference transcribed from the official layer, with weights read straight from the checkpoint shards:

| layer | attention cos / rel err | MoE cos / rel err |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.99999 / 0.004 | 0.738 / 0.94 |
| 1 | 0.99999 / 0.005 | 0.608 / 0.80 |
| 31 | 0.99999 / 0.003 | 0.166 / 1.02 |

- Inside the MoE everything feeding the kernel was correct: router logits matched exactly, top-k ids agreed 100%, and every expert `w13`/`w2` shard and the shared MLP weights matched the checkpoint slices. That left execution order, and `FusedMoE` turned out to be in place.

## Accuracy Tests

CPU unit tests in `test_hunyuan_image3_tp_broadcast.py`, all 11 in the file pass:
- Fix regressions: the shared MLP sees the layer input when the experts run in place; timesteps follow the official schedule. With only the two fixed source files reverted, exactly these two fail.
- Prefix cache: a cached suffix-only step matches full recompute; CFG slots do not overwrite each other; the prefix ends at the first varying token and is `None` when a clean image block straddles it.
- FA3 segments: segment attention equals masked SDPA for full and suffix-only steps; overlapping blocks fall back.
- Image API: `cot_text` and `bot_task` reach the sampling params.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

main + the fix vs this PR (prefix cache + fix), 2x H200 TP2 per the cookbook recipe, 1024x1024, 50 steps, guidance 2.5, seed 42. One warmup then one timed request per prompt.

| | main + fix | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| short prompt, request | 34.97 s | 27.42 s | -21.6% (1.28x) |
| short prompt, AR/denoise stage | 34.19 s | 26.68 s | -22.0% |
| long prompt, request | 35.84 s | 27.49 s | -23.3% (1.30x) |
| long prompt, AR/denoise stage | 35.04 s | 26.75 s | -23.7% |
| peak memory (server log) | 106,318 MB | 106,318 MB | no change |
| output vs main + fix | | byte-identical on both prompts | PSNR inf |

Images and notes are in the results comment. Earlier numbers and the noise-texture images in older comments were taken before the fix and should be ignored.

## Checklist

- [x] Format with pre-commit hooks (ruff F401/F821/F823/UP037, ruff-format)
- [x] Unit tests added (fix regressions + prefix cache)
- [x] GPU time / memory / parity on the fixed code
- [ ] Docs / cookbook update (the CUDA recipe could move from unverified once the numbers are in)

**How it was localized** (2x H200, TP2, debug-only instrumentation, not in this PR)

- Checked the port line by line against the official `modeling_hunyuan_image_3.py` and `hunyuan_image_3_pipeline.py` shipped with the checkpoint: 2D RoPE, QKV split, QK norm order, SwiGLU half order, residual flow, UNetDown/UNetUp, timestep embedders, CFG, Euler step and VAE decode all match.

| layer | attention cos / rel err | MoE cos / rel err |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.99999 / 0.004 | 0.738 / 0.94 |
| 1 | 0.99999 / 0.005 | 0.608 / 0.80 |
| 31 | 0.99999 / 0.003 | 0.166 / 1.02 |

- Inside the MoE everything that feeds the kernel was correct: router logits matched exactly, top-k ids agreed 100%, and every expert `w13`/`w2` shard and the shared MLP weights matched the checkpoint slices. That left execution order, and `FusedMoE` turned out to be in place.

1. Run the shared MLP before the in-place experts.

**Cache size:** 156 MB per GPU for a 1,248-token prefix with both CFG slots. That is exactly `32 layers x (K, V) x 4 kv heads per rank x 128 x 2 bytes x 1,248 tokens x 2 slots`, and the reported peak memory did not change.

**Batched requests with different prompt lengths:** two concurrent requests (short + long prompt) were batched by the server into one 4-row forward (padded to 5,472 tokens, shared prefix 1,248). ### Optional FA3 attention: benchmark (opt-in via `--attention-backend fa3`) Branch: [`wip/hunyuan-image3-fa3-segments`](https://github.com/OnePunchMonk/sglang/tree/wip/hunyuan-image3-fa3-segments) (2273a3aa95, on top of this PR) **What it does.** The HunyuanImage-3 mask is causal text plus bidirectional image blocks. GQA is native, so the `repeat_kv` copies go away too. Works for both the full step 0 and the cached suffix steps. ### TP4 check 4x H200, `--tp-size 4`, 1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG 2.5, seed 42, default attention (SDPA). Time = `HunyuanImage3AR finished in`. Both trees include the `cot_text` fix. TP4 changes the all-reduce order, so parity is checked against a TP4 baseline, not the TP2 images. | request | prefix / seq tokens | main + fix (TP4) | this PR (TP4) | speedup | output vs main + fix | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | short | 1,248 / 5,348 | 19.41 s | 15.23 s | 1.27x | PSNR 35.0 dB | | long | 1,372 / 5,472 | 20.26 s | 15.15 s | 1.34x | PSNR 25.2 dB | | think, ~1,000 token reasoning | 2,262 / 6,362 | 24.32 s | 15.91 s | 1.53x | PSNR 40.2 dB | Peak memory per GPU: 67,774 MB vs 67,818-67,836 MB (+44-62 MB; the cache is half the TP2 size per GPU since kv heads are split 4 ways). **Not bitwise at TP4 with the stock all-reduce, but the cache itself is exact.** At TP2 this PR is bitwise identical to main + fix; at TP4 with the default all-reduce it is not (PSNR 25-40 dB, same composition, small detail drift). To confirm, I reran both trees at TP4 with a debug-only all-reduce (all-gather, then sum in fixed rank order, so the order no longer depends on offset or message size). So at TP>2 the outputs differ from main + fix only at the same level as any change in all-reduce order (for example a different message size or NCCL version), not because of the cache. | | main + fix (TP4) | this PR (TP4) | |---|---|---| | short | | | | long | | | | think | | | Prompts are the same as the earlier comments: short `A blue ceramic teapot on a wooden table, soft daylight.`, long is the reading-nook prompt, think is the teapot prompt with the ~1,000 token reasoning text.

Two runs on 4x H200, `--tp-size 4`, 1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG 2.5, seed 42, default attention (SDPA), main + fix vs this PR (both with the `cot_text` fix). Full tables and images: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46454#issuecomment-6423193507

**1. Stock all-reduce (what users run)**

| request | prefix / seq tokens | main + fix | this PR | speedup | output |

| short | 1,248 / 5,348 | 19.41 s | 15.23 s | 1.27x | PSNR 35.0 dB |

**2. Fixed-order all-reduce (debug only, not in this PR)**

Both trees patched so the TP all-reduce is an all-gather followed by a sum in fixed rank order, which makes the summation order independent of message size and buffer offset.

| request | main + fix | this PR | output |

The drift in run 1 comes from the all-reduce summation order: NCCL's ring all-reduce orders each element's 4-way sum by its offset in the buffer, and suffix-only steps all-reduce fewer token rows, so the same row lands at a different offset. detail.body:
## Motivation

Depends on #46600 (the CUDA MoE noise fix, which fixes #46461). This PR will be rebased on it once it lands, so the fix commit below will drop out of the diff.

Changes for HunyuanImage-3 (the prefix K/V cache is the main one; the opt-in FA3 attention and the `cot_text` fix are described under Modifications):

1. **Fix: generation on CUDA produced a noise texture** (on main too). The MoE block ran the routed experts before the shared MLP. On CUDA the Triton `FusedMoE` path runs in place (`inplace=True` by default) and overwrites `hidden_states` with the expert output, so the shared MLP read the expert output instead of the layer input and every MoE layer was wrong. The NPU path (AscendTPDispatcher) is not in place, which is likely why the original NPU validation in #36311 did not see it; the cookbook also marks the CUDA recipe as unverified. srt's own Hunyuan model already runs the shared MLP first.
2. **Perf: cache the text prefix K/V across denoising steps.** HunyuanImage-3 recomputes the whole text prefix through every layer (attention and MoE) on every step, even though that prefix never changes. The proposal this implements:

> **P1. Prefix KV cache** (`hunyuan_image3.py`: `ImageKVCacheManager`, `forward_block`)
> The text prefix is causal and step-invariant. At `first_step`, keep the per-layer prefix K/V; on later steps feed only the image tokens as queries and attend to [cached prefix K/V, image K/V]. Replace the dense 4-D bool-mask SDPA with FA varlen (prefix causal + image full) or flex.
> Removes L_text/(L_text+L_img) of the MoE compute per step. Large for long or "think" prompts; also recovers FlashAttention.

This PR does the prefix K/V cache with the dense SDPA as the default, plus the FA varlen part as an opt-in (`--attention-backend fa3`), since FA3 is not bitwise equal to SDPA. The official model does the same caching at inference (later steps feed only the timestep and image tokens against a static KV cache).

## Modifications

**Fix (commit 2)**
- `hunyuan_image3.py`: `HunYuanSparseMoeBlock.forward` runs the shared MLP before the in-place experts.
- `pipelines/hunyuan_image3.py`: match the official `FlowMatchDiscreteScheduler` schedule, `shift(linspace(1, 0, N + 1))[:-1]` (`use_uniform_sigmas=True`). The old setup shifted the training-sigma range a second time; for 10 steps the last timestep was 8.93 instead of 250.

**Prefix K/V cache (commit 1)**
- `hunyuan_image3_utils.py`: `ImageKVCacheManager` stores each layer's prefix K/V on step 0, keyed by a cache slot, and on later steps prepends it to the suffix K/V. Adds `split_suffix_inputs` and `pad_prefix_rows`.
- `hunyuan_image3.py`: `forward_block` takes `prefix_len` and `cache_slot`. Step 0 runs the full sequence; later steps run only the suffix rows and pad the output back to full length, so callers see the same shape.
- `ar_stage.py`: computes the prefix once as the rows before the first noisy-image or timestep token, and returns no prefix (full compute) when a clean image block straddles that boundary. `first_step` is now `step_idx == 0` (it was always `True`, and nothing read it). CFG cond and uncond use separate cache slots, since they run as two backbone calls on the same modules.
- Falls back to the current path when CLA is on, when the cache-dit adapter drives the blocks, or when no safe prefix exists.

Why the cache is exact: the mask is causal, so every row before the first varying token only sees prompt and clean conditioning tokens. Clean conditioning images before the noisy block are cached too, so the saving is a bit larger than L_text/(L_text+L_img).

Memory cost of the cache: `bs x P x kv_heads x head_dim x 4 bytes` per layer per CFG slot. Measured 156 MB per GPU for a 1,248-token prefix with both CFG slots (exactly the formula); the reported peak is unchanged.

**Opt-in FA3 segment attention (`--attention-backend fa3`)**
- `hunyuan_image3_utils.py`: `build_attention_segments` splits the mask (causal text, bidirectional image blocks) into `(start, end, causal)` segments; `segmented_attention` runs one FA3 varlen call per segment with bottom-right causal alignment, for both full and cached-suffix steps. GQA is native, so no `repeat_kv`. Hopper only; elsewhere the masked SDPA path is kept.
- `ar_stage.py` / `pipelines/hunyuan_image3.py`: segments are built only when `attention_backend == "fa"` (what `fa3`/`fa4` resolve to). The default path is unchanged and still bitwise identical to main + fix.
- 2x H200: 22.6 s vs 26.8 s for the default path (1.55x vs main + fix). Not bitwise: PSNR 21-24 dB vs SDPA, same composition. On GPU the segments reproduce the attention mask exactly over 384 calls and FA3 vs SDPA differs by at most one bf16 ulp per call, so the drift is kernel rounding compounding over layers and steps. Details and images: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46454#issuecomment-6422227024

**Fix: `cot_text` from the image API**
- `configs/sample/hunyuan_image3.py`: declare `bot_task`, `system_prompt` and `cot_text` in `image_request_extra_fields`. The image endpoint only forwards declared fields, so think/recaption text was silently dropped. With it, think prompts are 1.32x to 1.50x faster than main + fix (the reasoning text lands in the cached prefix), outputs identical: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46454#issuecomment-6422648092

## How the noise bug was found

On 2x H200 TP2 with debug-only instrumentation (not in this PR):
- Checked the port line by line against the official `modeling_hunyuan_image_3.py` and `hunyuan_image_3_pipeline.py` shipped with the checkpoint. 2D RoPE, QKV split, QK norm order, SwiGLU half order, residual flow, UNetDown/UNetUp, timestep embedders, CFG, Euler step and VAE decode all match.
- Compared real decoder layers at step 0 against an fp32 reference transcribed from the official layer, with weights read straight from the checkpoint shards:

| layer | attention cos / rel err | MoE cos / rel err |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.99999 / 0.004 | 0.738 / 0.94 |
| 1 | 0.99999 / 0.005 | 0.608 / 0.80 |
| 31 | 0.99999 / 0.003 | 0.166 / 1.02 |

- Inside the MoE everything feeding the kernel was correct: router logits matched exactly, top-k ids agreed 100%, and every expert `w13`/`w2` shard and the shared MLP weights matched the checkpoint slices. That left execution order, and `FusedMoE` turned out to be in place.

## Accuracy Tests

CPU unit tests in `test_hunyuan_image3_tp_broadcast.py`, all 11 in the file pass:
- Fix regressions: the shared MLP sees the layer input when the experts run in place; timesteps follow the official schedule. With only the two fixed source files reverted, exactly these two fail.
- Prefix cache: a cached suffix-only step matches full recompute; CFG slots do not overwrite each other; the prefix ends at the first varying token and is `None` when a clean image block straddles it.
- FA3 segments: segment attention equals masked SDPA for full and suffix-only steps; overlapping blocks fall back.
- Image API: `cot_text` and `bot_task` reach the sampling params.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

main + the fix vs this PR (prefix cache + fix), 2x H200 TP2 per the cookbook recipe, 1024x1024, 50 steps, guidance 2.5, seed 42. One warmup then one timed request per prompt.

**Root cause**

`HunYuanSparseMoeBlock.forward` ran the routed experts before the shared MLP. On CUDA the Triton `FusedMoE` path runs in place (`inplace=True` by default) and overwrites `hidden_states` with the expert output, so the shared MLP then read the expert output instead of the layer input. Every MoE layer was wrong. The NPU path (AscendTPDispatcher) is not in place, which is likely why the original NPU validation in #36311 did not see it. srt's own Hunyuan model already runs the shared MLP first.

**How it was localized** (2x H200, TP2, debug-only instrumentation, not in this PR)

- Checked the port line by line against the official `modeling_hunyuan_image_3.py` and `hunyuan_image_3_pipeline.py` shipped with the checkpoint: 2D RoPE, QKV split, QK norm order, SwiGLU half order, residual flow, UNetDown/UNetUp, timestep embedders, CFG, Euler step and VAE decode all match.
- Compared real decoder layers at step 0 against an fp32 reference transcribed from the official layer, with weights read straight from the checkpoint shards:

| layer | attention cos / rel err | MoE cos / rel err |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.99999 / 0.004 | 0.738 / 0.94 |
| 1 | 0.99999 / 0.005 | 0.608 / 0.80 |
| 31 | 0.99999 / 0.003 | 0.166 / 1.02 |

- Inside the MoE everything that feeds the kernel was correct: router logits matched exactly, top-k ids agreed 100%, and every expert `w13`/`w2` shard and the shared MLP weights matched the checkpoint slices. That left execution order, and `FusedMoE` turned out to be in place.

**Fixes in 6aa0fc0ba8**

1. Run the shared MLP before the in-place experts.
2. Match the official timestep schedule, `shift(linspace(1, 0, N + 1))[:-1]` (`use_uniform_sigmas=True`). The old setup shifted the training-sigma range a second time, e.g. for 10 steps the last timestep was 8.93 instead of 250.
3. Two regression tests in `test_hunyuan_image3_tp_broadcast.py`. On CPU, all 9 tests in the file pass; with only the two source files reverted to the previous version, exactly these two fail.

Also noticed: the official model already does prefix K/V caching at inference (later steps feed only the timestep and image tokens against a static KV cache), which is the same idea as the first commit here.

### Optional FA3 attention: benchmark (opt-in via `--attention-backend fa3`) Branch: [`wip/hunyuan-image3-fa3-segments`](https://github.com/OnePunchMonk/sglang/tree/wip/hunyuan-image3-fa3-segments) (2273a3aa95, on top of this PR) **What it does.** The HunyuanImage-3 mask is causal text plus bidirectional image blocks. That splits exactly into a few mask-free FA3 varlen calls (causal per text run, non-causal per image block), so the dense 4-D bool-mask SDPA (memory-efficient cutlass kernel, ~20% of a step) is skipped. GQA is native, so the `repeat_kv` copies go away too. Works for both the full step 0 and the cached suffix steps. Hopper only; other GPUs keep SDPA. **Setup.** 2x H200, TP2, 1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG 2.5, seed 42, same server build, timing = `HunyuanImage3AR finished in` (2 runs each, identical). | | short prompt | long prompt | vs main + fix | |---|---|---|---| | main + fix (SDPA, no cache) | 34.97 s | 35.84 s | 1.00x | | this PR, default (SDPA + prefix cache) | 26.75 s | 26.78-27.32 s | 1.31x | | this PR + `--attention-backend fa3` | 22.58 s | 22.60 s | **1.55x** | FA3 adds ~1.18x on top of the prefix cache. Per step: backbone ~440 ms vs ~525 ms, attention ~20 ms vs ~96 ms. **Why opt-in.** FA3 is not bitwise equal to masked SDPA, so outputs drift: | | default vs main + fix | fa3 vs main + fix | |---|---|---| | short | identical (bitwise) | mean abs diff 9.7/255, PSNR 21.2 dB | | long | identical (bitwise) | mean abs diff 7.3/255, PSNR 23.6 dB | To check this is kernel rounding and not a bug, I compared every attention call of a real request (384 calls: warmup, full step and suffix steps) on GPU: the segments reproduce the attention mask exactly (0 mismatches), and FA3 vs SDPA differs by at most 0.0078 (one bf16 ulp near 1.0), mean ~1e-5. That per-call rounding compounds over 32 layers x 50 steps into visible detail changes, but composition and quality are the same (images below). FA3 runs are deterministic (reruns identical). Since this PR is meant to be lossless, the default stays on SDPA and FA3 is opt-in through the existing `--attention-backend fa3` flag. One more thing to know: with FA3, a request batched with a shorter one is no longer bitwise identical to running it alone (the shared prefix length changes the per-segment call shapes). With the default path it still is. **Prompts** - short: `A blue ceramic teapot on a wooden table, soft daylight.` - long: `A cozy reading nook inside an old stone cottage at dusk: a deep green velvet armchair beside a tall arched window, rain streaking the glass, a brass floor lamp casting warm amber light, a knitted wool blanket draped over the armrest, a stack of leather-bound books on a small oak side table next to a steaming ceramic mug of tea, a sleeping orange tabby cat curled on a round cushion, shelves of books and trailing potted ivy along the walls, a faded persian rug on wide wooden floorboards, soft shadows, shallow depth of field, rich textures, photorealistic, 35mm film look, calm and inviting atmosphere.` | | default (SDPA, = main + fix) | `--attention-backend fa3` | |---|---|---| | short | | | | long | | | Happy to fold this into the PR as an opt-in, or send it as a follow-up, whichever is easier to review.

### TP4 check 4x H200, `--tp-size 4`, 1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG 2.5, seed 42, default attention (SDPA). Time = `HunyuanImage3AR finished in`. Both trees include the `cot_text` fix. TP4 changes the all-reduce order, so parity is checked against a TP4 baseline, not the TP2 images. | request | prefix / seq tokens | main + fix (TP4) | this PR (TP4) | speedup | output vs main + fix | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | short | 1,248 / 5,348 | 19.41 s | 15.23 s | 1.27x | PSNR 35.0 dB | | long | 1,372 / 5,472 | 20.26 s | 15.15 s | 1.34x | PSNR 25.2 dB | | think, ~1,000 token reasoning | 2,262 / 6,362 | 24.32 s | 15.91 s | 1.53x | PSNR 40.2 dB | Peak memory per GPU: 67,774 MB vs 67,818-67,836 MB (+44-62 MB; the cache is half the TP2 size per GPU since kv heads are split 4 ways). **Not bitwise at TP4 with the stock all-reduce, but the cache itself is exact.** At TP2 this PR is bitwise identical to main + fix; at TP4 with the default all-reduce it is not (PSNR 25-40 dB, same composition, small detail drift). The cause is the all-reduce summation order, not the cache: - With 2 ranks every element is `a + b`, which is order independent, so TP2 is always exact. - With 4 ranks each element sums 4 partials, and NCCL's ring all-reduce picks the order from the element's offset in the buffer. Suffix-only steps all-reduce fewer token rows, so the same row sits at a different offset and gets a different summation order. To confirm, I reran both trees at TP4 with a debug-only all-reduce (all-gather, then sum in fixed rank order, so the order no longer depends on offset or message size). With that, this PR is **bitwise identical** to main + fix on all three prompts (short, long, think). Timing in that run is not meaningful (the debug all-reduce is slower), but the ratio held: 22.47 s -> 17.62 s, 23.39 s -> 17.49 s, 27.84 s -> 18.16 s. So at TP>2 the outputs differ from main + fix only at the same level as any change in all-reduce order (for example a different message size or NCCL version), not because of the cache. | | main + fix (TP4) | this PR (TP4) | |---|---|---| | short | | | | long | | | | think | | | Prompts are the same as the earlier comments: short `A blue ceramic teapot on a wooden table, soft daylight.`, long is the reading-nook prompt, think is the teapot prompt with the ~1,000 token reasoning text.

### TP > 2 tests (summary)

Two runs on 4x H200, `--tp-size 4`, 1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG 2.5, seed 42, default attention (SDPA), main + fix vs this PR (both with the `cot_text` fix). Full tables and images: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46454#issuecomment-6423193507

**1. Stock all-reduce (what users run)**

| request | prefix / seq tokens | main + fix | this PR | speedup | output |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| short | 1,248 / 5,348 | 19.41 s | 15.23 s | 1.27x | PSNR 35.0 dB |
| long | 1,372 / 5,472 | 20.26 s | 15.15 s | 1.34x | PSNR 25.2 dB |
| think, ~1,000 token reasoning | 2,262 / 6,362 | 24.32 s | 15.91 s | 1.53x | PSNR 40.2 dB |

Peak memory +44-62 MB per GPU (the cache, split 4 ways). Outputs keep the same composition but are not bitwise identical, unlike TP2.

**2. Fixed-order all-reduce (debug only, not in this PR)**

Both trees patched so the TP all-reduce is an all-gather followed by a sum in fixed rank order, which makes the summation order independent of message size and buffer offset.

| request | main + fix | this PR | output |
|---|---|---|---|
| short | 22.47 s | 17.62 s | **bitwise identical** |
| long | 23.39 s | 17.49 s | **bitwise identical** |
| think | 27.84 s | 18.16 s | **bitwise identical** |

**Conclusion.** The prefix cache is exact at TP4. The drift in run 1 comes from the all-reduce summation order: NCCL's ring all-reduce orders each element's 4-way sum by its offset in the buffer, and suffix-only steps all-reduce fewer token rows, so the same row lands at a different offset. With 2 ranks each element is just `a + b`, which is order independent, which is why TP2 is bitwise exact with the stock all-reduce.
